movement_source: row 'Common Equity Tier 1 (APRA) (%)', column 30 Jun 20 (Full Year Ended) -> column 30 Jun 21 (Full Year Ended)
headline: CBA's APRA Level 2 CET1 ratio rose 150 bpts, from 11.6% at 30 Jun 20 to 13.1% at 30 Jun 21, well above APRA's 'unquestionably strong' 10.5% benchmark (ev-55, ev-2, ev-62). CET1 capital grew $52,551m to $58,836m while total RWA fell 1% to $450,680m from $454,948m (ev-41, ev-57). CBA's own FY20→FY21 walk attributes the move to cash NPAT (+88 bpts 2H20, +97 bpts 2H21), divestments (+42), the APRA operational risk add-on reduction (+17), RWA (-13 then +8) and other (-2 then +4), less dividends (-32 and -59) (ev-49). The internationally comparable CET1 ratio — a different measure — rose 200 bpts to 19.4% (ev-56). The FY21 dividend was 350c, up 17%, totalling $6,209m against $5,275m (ev-58, ev-60). A $6.0bn off-market buy-back was announced but sits after the balance date, reducing the ratio only pro-forma to 12.1–12.2% (ev-65, ev-26).

drivers.columns: Jun 20 to Dec 20 (+88) and Dec 20 to Jun 21 (+97)
drivers.narrative: The dominant driver. CBA's FY20→FY21 walk prints Cash NPAT of +88 bpts in 2H20 and +97 bpts in 2H21 (ev-49). Cash NPAT was $8,653m, up 19.8% on FY20, as "improved economic conditions and outlook" cut loan impairment expense 78% to $554m (ev-63, ev-64). Net retained earnings rose $30,811m to $36,558m (ev-70). Excludes equity-accounted associate profits, which are capital neutral (ev-3).

drivers.columns: Jun 20 to Dec 20 (-32) and Dec 20 to Jun 21 (-59)
drivers.narrative: Two dividend payments fall inside the window: the 2020 final dividend (-32 bpts), whose DRP was satisfied by issuing $264m of shares at a 15.2% participation rate, and the 2021 interim dividend (-59 bpts), whose DRP was neutralised in full by the on-market purchase of $418m of shares, itself costing 9 bpts (ev-49, ev-6, ev-4, ev-53). FY21 dividends totalled $6,209m (350c) versus $5,275m (298c) (ev-60, ev-58).

CBA prints +42 bpts for divestments in the FY20→FY21 walk (ev-49). CET1 capital was "supported by ... the benefits of proceeds received from the sales of BoCommLife, CommInsure Life, and other previously announced divestments" (ev-31). BoCommLife completed Dec 20, CommInsure Life Apr 21, Aussie Home Loans and AUSIEX May 21; completed divestments carry a combined CET1 uplift of +175 bpts (ev-67). Final CommInsure Life proceeds (+2 bpts) sit in the 2H21 Other bar (ev-5).

Reflects "APRA's announcement on 20 November 2020 resulting in a 50% reduction in CBA's operational RWA add-on (from $12.5bn to $6.25bn)" (ev-50, ev-49). Operational risk RWA fell from $57,212m at Jun 20 to $46,204m at Jun 21 (ev-34); the results book adds that a $6.25bn APRA add-on remained at 30 Jun 2021 and that further decline came from "improvements in the Group's operational risk profile", enhanced conduct risk management and simplification from divestments.

drivers.columns: Jun 20 to Dec 20 (-13) and Dec 20 to Jun 21 (+8)
drivers.narrative: The walk prints Underlying RWA -13 bpts in 2H20 and RWA +8 bpts in 2H21 (ev-49) — a small net drag once the separately-shown APRA add-on release is stripped out. Total RWA fell 1% to $450,680m from $454,948m (ev-57). Within that, credit risk RWA rose 2% to $381,550m (residential mortgage AIRB RWA $148,294m to $159,758m) and IRRBB rose $11,085m to $14,619m, offset by traded market risk falling $12,457m to $8,307m (ev-59, ev-38, ev-37, ev-36).

drivers.columns: Jun 20 to Dec 20 (-2) and Dec 20 to Jun 21 (+4)
drivers.narrative: Other regulatory adjustments were -2 bpts in 2H20 and +4 bpts in 2H21 (ev-49). The 2H21 bar "includes receipt of the final proceeds from the sale of CommInsure Life (CET1 impact of 2 basis points)" (ev-5, ev-47). Behind the line, equity investment deductions grew from $(3,648)m to $(6,782)m and CET1 capital before regulatory adjustments rose $71,661m to $78,239m (ev-42, ev-71).

drivers.columns: Not in FY20-FY21 walk; pro-forma only
drivers.narrative: The $6.0bn off-market share buy-back contributed nothing to the FY21 ratio: it sits outside the Jun 20 → Jun 21 walk (ev-49) and is shown only after the Jun 21 Level 2 endpoint, taking the pro-forma ratio to 12.1–12.2% with expected divestment uplift of 39–49 bpts (ev-26, ev-27, ev-54). CBA states "Post buy-back, CBA will continue to have a significant capital surplus", from $11.5bn reported (ev-27, ev-65).

notable_items: FY21 loan impairment expense fell 78% to $554m on improved economic conditions and outlook, the main lift to earnings-generated capital (ev-64)
APRA's 20 November 2020 decision halved CBA's operational risk RWA add-on from $12.5bn to $6.25bn, a one-off +17 bpts regulatory benefit inside the window (ev-50)
$6.0bn off-market share buy-back announced with the FY21 result but effected after 30 June 2021 - pro-forma Jun 21 Level 2 ratio 12.1-12.2% (ev-65, ev-26)
Expected further CET1 uplift of 39-49 bpts from the Colonial First State and CommInsure General Insurance divestments, not yet in the FY21 ratio (ev-54)

disagreements.topic: Divestments and organic bars in the FY20-FY21 CET1 walk
values: Divestments +42, Cash NPAT +88/+97, RWA -13/+8, Other -2/+4, Dividends -32/-59 (presentation p111)
disagreements.preferred: Divestments +42 with the half-by-half decomposition (presentation p111)
disagreements.explanation: Both slides walk Jun 20 (11.6%) to Jun 21 (13.1%) and both sum to +150 bpts, but p37 aggregates into a single 'Organic (net of growth / investment, ex dividends)' bar of +180 that bundles cash NPAT with RWA and other movements, and assigns +44 to divestments. The appendix p111 chart decomposes the same +150 by half and by component, giving divestments +42. I adopt p111 as the finer framing of the same comparison; the 2 bpt divestment difference is presentational.

The task and CBA's own headline use the APRA Level 2 (Group) ratio from the results book KPI table (ev-55). The internationally comparable ratio (+200 bpts) and the Level 1 ratio are different measures, quoted only as context.

limitations: The results book (profit announcement) publishes only a HALF-ON-HALF CET1 walk (Dec 20 to Jun 21: +97 cash NPAT, +8 RWA, +4 other, -59 dividend, ev-7). No FY20-to-FY21 walk appears in the results book, so the driver table is built from the results PRESENTATION appendix (p111), a slide - one rung lower in the source hierarchy.

The adopted p111 walk decomposes the year via the Dec 20 intermediate point, so each driver is the sum of two half-year bars rather than a single bank-stated full-year contribution. The endpoints and the +150 bpt total are the task's own, and the bars sum to +150.

CBA calls its p37 aggregate bar 'Organic (net of growth / investment, ex dividends)' (+180 bpts): a NET number in which franchise growth and investment spend are already offset against earnings, so the gross earnings contribution is larger than any single bar shows (ev-28, ev-27).

The Cash NPAT bars explicitly EXCLUDE net equity accounted profits from associates, 'as they are capital neutral with offsetting increases in regulatory capital deductions' (ev-3), so that earnings stream appears in neither the earnings nor the deductions driver.

No document gives a bpts split of the RWA bars between credit, market, operational and IRRBB risk on an FY21-vs-FY20 basis; the RWA driver narrative uses the $M levels from the capital note (ev-33, ev-59) and the bpts split published on p35 of the presentation is a half-on-half figure and is not used.
The 2H20 half of the walk (Jun 20 to Dec 20) is not itself the task comparison; it is used only as a component of the full-year span, consistent with the walk CBA publishes.

Capped at 80: earnings_generation +185 bps, dividend_net_drp -91 bps, rwa -5 bps, capital_returns +0 bps. The records these claims cite do not state those numbers, so each one is arithmetic over the evidence rather than a figure read from it.

The Group’s CET1 ratio (APRA) was 13.1% as at 30 June 2021, an increase of 50 basis points from 31 December 2020 and an increase of 150 basis points from 30 June 2020.

Key drivers of the change in CET1 for the 6 months ended 30 June 2021 were capital generated from earnings (+97 basis points, excluding net equity accounted profits from associates), lower total RWA (+8 basis points) and other regulatory adjustments (+4 basis points), partly offset by the 2021 interim dividend (-59 basis points)
